question: In order to carry out surveillance in the pre-frontier area, Frontex also uses satellite images. In 2020, the EUROSUR Fusion Service (EFS) delivered 409 optical images and 1 163 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images to end users; in 2021, this figure was around twice as high. 1.
How many satellite images (optical and SAR) did the EFS process in 2022, 2023 and 2024, and how many anomaly detection alerts were generated on that basis?
How many ‘vessels of interest’ were under surveillance, and how many reports were produced as a result?
What kind of technology is being used to track ‘vessels of interest’, and what enhancements regarding high-resolution sensors have been introduced by Frontex or the EU Satellite Centre since 2021?
answer: As the question regarding ‘Satellite-based Eurosur surveillance in the pre-frontier area from 2022 onwards’ falls under the responsibility of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), the Commission has asked the Agency to provide the details requested by the Honourable Member. The Agency’s reply will be sent by the Commission to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.
The EU Satellite Centre (SatCen) is not involved in the provision of Eurosur Fusion Services by Frontex to end users.

With respect to the enhancements introduced by SatCen regarding high-resolution sensors, according to Council Decision 2014/401/CFSP, SatCen provides ‘products and services resulting from the exploitation of relevant space assets and collateral data, including satellite and aerial imagery, and related services’.

In order to achieve its mandate, SatCen does not only make use of the Copernicus earth observation satellites and Copernicus contributing missions but other commercial very high-resolution satellites as well.

As a consequence, the main enhancement as regards the use of high-resolution sensors in SatCen is that it incorporated into its portfolio new very high-resolution satellite sensors available on the market, after properly testing and validating their capabilities. See annexes: Annex 1, Annex 2, Annex 3.
